thread:
incident-bot: Pager: alert: prod 5xx rate spike in eu-west and us-west (p95 latency stable). paging @oncall-sre & @oncall-platform.

marco: ack. i'm oncall. looking. any deploys in last 30m?

jen: saw a blue/green push for `routing-service` ~5m ago, feature flag `new-routingv2` enabled for 20% traffic by deploy pipeline.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15_09:12: blue->green rollout started (routing-service) by @jen. canary: eu-west(10%), us-west(10%). full rollout scheduled.

sasha: i'm seeing canary 502s in eu-west: 502 from upstream `router` with body "upstream reset". 5xx rate jump from 0.2% -> 6.8% over 4m.

rick: logs: `router` logs show connection refused to `model-proxy:443` on the green pool. stack traces attached to log group. short snippet:
```
ERROR router: upstream connect error: connection refused, peer=10.2.8.14:443
at proxy/connection.cc:142
```

marco: sounds like green instances are failing healthchecks, traffic still routed -> 5xx. can we disable the feature flag for the rollout? kill-switch first.

jen: trying feature-flags api now. toggling `new-routingv2` -> OFF for rollout group id=2026-03-15.

jen: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"new-routingv2","state":"off","scope":"rollout-2026-03-15"}'` -> 200 OK.

deploy-bot: feature flag change propagated to control plane.

sasha: still seeing ~3.2% 5xx in eu-west, us-west trending down slowly. some clients still hitting green IPs.

danny: possible DNS/edge cache. note that blue/green uses weighted DNS + LB. when flag toggled we expected immediate switch at Layer7 but DNS TTL 60s + CDN cache might keep routes for a bit. dig from different regions:
```
$ dig +short routing.service.prod.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
52.12.33.1  (blue)
52.12.33.1  (blue)
54.23.11.9  (green)
```

marco: ah — some resolvers still returning green A record. could be partial DNS propagation or stale LB. can we shift LB weights to 100% blue as emergency?

jen: opening emergency LB manual override. hitting console to set weights.

jen: `lb set-weight routing-service eu-west blue=100 green=0` -> accepted. same for us-west.

deploy-bot: LB weight change applied to edge routers.

rick: after weight flip, 5xx dropped to 0.4% in eu-west within ~45s. us-west similar. still a handful of 502s from older clients (ISP caches).

product-liz: we have 14 customer reports in Zendesk mentioning failures for short period. pushing a brief status update.

cust-ops-bot: Noted. Outbound: statuspage updated: partial outage for routing-service impacting some customers; mitigation in progress.

marco: root cause initial triage: green instances in canary failing upstream connection to model-proxy due to TLS mismatch from a miscompiled proxy image (regression in green). rollout started while some resolvers were still returning green due to DNS + LB hybrid, causing customer-facing 5xx spike.

sasha: actions taken: 1) feature flag kill-switch off 2) LB weights forced to blue=100 3) rolled back green deploy images from canary pools 4) cleared CDN route cache for known POPs 5) status updates.

jen: rollback command executed: `deploy rollback routing-service --to=2026-03-14-2145 --scope=canary` -> deploy-bot reports rollback completed, instances drained and replaced with previous image.

deploy-bot: rollback complete. all canary hosts in eu-west and us-west show healthy=10/10.

rick: verified with synthetic traffic and curl from multiple regions:
```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://routing.service.prod.redwood.com/health
200 0.123
```

marco: paging summary: incident acknowledged 2100123456 -> mitigated 2100123720. residual customer errors cleared by 2100123780. total customer impact window ~18m.

danny: follow-up items assigned: - SRE: audit deploy pipeline to ensure pre-rollout canary healthchecks include TLS smoke tests (owner: rick) - Platform: ensure LB weight fallback triggers faster on flag toggles (owner: jen) - Dev: revert proxy image regression and add e2e for TLS (owner: sasha) - Docs: update runbook about DNS/TTL implications for blue/green (owner: marco).

marco: handing off to next oncall @sasha for midnight watch and postmortem. key artifacts: logs uploaded to s3://incidents/2100123456/, deploy diff: sha abcd1234 -> ef56gh78, rollback ticket created #INC-4829.

sasha: ack. i'll take follow-ups and start the postmortem draft. leaving channel open for 1h for any additional context. :clipboard: :white_check_mark:

jen: thanks everyone. good triage. we should also look at making the flag toggle emit a non-ambiguous traffic cut when set to off for rollout scopes (tech debt).

incident-bot: Incident state -> RESOLVED (mitigated). severity: S2. postmortem owner: sasha.

marco: closing thread. if you added anything to the postmortem bucket, ping me.
